Step 6.5: inbound Disruptor wiring (SRS §3.2)
Add the inbound ring buffer so Step 7 has a buffer to produce into.
- pom: add com.lmax:disruptor:4.0.0 (compile scope) - OrderEventFactory: pre-allocates empty OrderEvent slots; isolates the sole com.lmax import in the event package (OrderEvent stays framework-free) - InboundPipeline: single-producer Disruptor<OrderEvent>, one consumer, BlockingWaitStrategy (demo default), 1024-slot ring; exposes the RingBuffer - CapturingOrderHandler (test): reusable snapshot-recording consumer for 6.5 and Step 7; copies fields out to survive slot reuse - InboundPipelineTest: distinct/empty slots, publish round-trip, and slot-reuse (size-1 ring) with no stale-field bleed

feat: implement order submission, cancellation, and book display
- addOrder: routes to matchBuy/matchSell, rests unfilled quantity - addToBook: inserts order into price level queue via computeIfAbsent - cancelOrder: marks order cancelled and removes from book with O(n) lookup - printBook: displays current bid/ask book state

- Static utility class with AtomicLong counters - Replaces hardcoded 0L trade IDs in matchBuy/matchSell
Finished the main logic.

Did some file restructuring to organize classes

Implemented step 0 of the order gateway: added FixConstants holding SOH = 0x01, EQUALS = '='. tag numbers: 8, 9, 10, 35, 11, 38, 41, 44, 54, 55. msg-type bytes: 'D', 'F'. the single configured instrument symbol for the book

Implemented step 1 of the order gateway:parseLong(byte[] buf, int start, int end). Goal: pure byte-range to long. Foundation for every numeric parse downstream. Walk bytes [start, end). For each: digit = b - '0', reject if outside 0..9, accumulate val = val * 10 + digit.As well as some unit tests

Add parsePrice for FIX price fields (Step 2)
Parse a byte-range FIX price to long cents, reusing parseLong for the integer and fractional parts. Scale the fraction by digit length, not value: one digit *10, two digits as-is.
Reject (-1L sentinel, consistent with parseLong) on: empty range, empty integer part, more than two decimals, non-digit bytes, and non-positive result. The zero/negative price policy is applied here via the > 0 check, since parseLong deliberately treats "0" as a valid parse.
PRICE_SCALE and MAX_DECIMALS kept private to the parser (no second caller). No String/split/BigDecimal; pure byte[] in, off the hot path.
Tested: integer-only, one/two decimals, leading zeros, zero-integer-part with positive fraction, and rejects for >2 decimals, zero, negative, bare dot, empty integer part, trailing dot, trailing junk, and multiple dots. Tests embed each price in a wider buffer to verify offset/length bounds.

Add zero-allocation FIX message scanner (Step 3)
- Add MAX_FIELDS = 32 constant to FixConstants to bound scanner arrays - Add parallel arrays (tags, valStarts, valEnds) to FixParser for allocation-free tokenisation; reuse across messages with no reset needed - Implement FixParser.scan(): tokenises a raw FIX byte buffer into (tag, valueStart, valueEnd) triples; returns field count or -1 on any structural reject (missing '=', unterminated value, non-digit tag, field overflow)

test(gateway): add FixParser tag scanner tests
Cover the Step 3 scanner: session tags pass through in order, '='-in-value delimited by SOH, empty/non-numeric tag and missing '=' rejects, empty value accepted (deferred to Step 5), MAX_FIELDS boundary both sides, and offset/length handling within a larger buffer.

Add checksum validation for FIX messages (Step 4)
Verify tag 10 before any message interpretation: sum every byte up to and including the SOH preceding "10=", mod 256, and compare against the field's three-digit value. Operates on raw byte[] so structural trust is established before the tag scan, independent of the Step 3 scanner arrays.
Locate the trailer by computing from the end (a complete message ends in the 7-byte 10=xxx<SOH>) rather than scanning for it, leaning on the frame decoder's trailer invariant instead of duplicating a scan. Read the three digits via parseLong, which gives free rejection of a malformed checksum field: its -1L sentinel can't equal a 0..255 sum, consistent with the parseLong/parsePrice reject convention.
Guard length < 8 (no room for a summed byte plus the trailer) before indexing. The per-byte & 0xFF is kept for clarity but is not load-bearing: the final & 0xFF already collapses the signed/unsigned difference, since a high byte differs by exactly 256, i.e. 0 mod 256.
Static, pure byte[] in; no String, no io.netty, no com.lmax. Runs at the gateway boundary, off the hot path.
Tested: known-good message (independently computed checksum), corrupted body byte, wrong checksum value, non-digit checksum field, too-short buffer, and the good message embedded in a wider buffer to verify offset/length bounds.

feat(gateway): implement FixParser.parse for 35=D and 35=F (Step 5)
Assemble the full message-level parser on top of the Step 1-4 primitives. parse() runs checksum -> scan -> dispatch on 35= -> per-type validation, populating a pre-allocated OrderEvent slot only on success.
- Add OrderEvent carrier and OrderEventType enum in event package (framework-free: no com.lmax/io.netty, so both parser and Disruptor can depend on it) - Add MSG_TYPE_NEW_ORDER ('D') / MSG_TYPE_CANCEL ('F') to FixConstants - Dispatch to parseNewOrder (requires 11,54,44,38,55) and parseCancel (requires 11,41) via thin switch on tag 35 - Validate into locals first; target is untouched on reject so the gateway only publishes valid messages - Clear message-type-specific fields per branch to avoid stale reads on the reused slot - eventType set in parser; timestamp deferred to gateway (Step 7) to keep parse deterministic and unit-testable - Add findTag, symbolMatches, mapSide helpers (zero-allocation) - Reject rules: non-numeric ClOrdID, invalid side (54=3), wrong symbol, qty <= 0 (38=0), bad price (0/negative/>2dp), unknown 35= type

test(gateway): add message-level tests for FixParser.parse (Step 5)
Cover the SRS Step 5 cases via a message builder that computes a correct BodyLength and CheckSum, so rejects are attributable to field validation rather than a bad trailer.
- valid 35=D (buy and sell) populates all fields; originalOrderId cleared - valid 35=F populates orderId/originalOrderId; side/price/quantity cleared - reject: missing tag 44, invalid side (54=3), wrong symbol, qty 0 (38=0), non-numeric ClOrdID, unknown 35= type

feat(gateway): add length-prefixed FixFrameDecoder
Step 6. First Netty-aware class in the parse path. Extends ByteToMessageDecoder, reads 9=<n>, emits one complete message (8=..<SOH> 9=<n><SOH> body 10=xxx<SOH>) at a time as a byte[] copy.
- frameLength/frameAndEmit are static, byte[]-only, Netty-free, so the framing math is unit-testable without EmbeddedChannel - handoff (a): frame copied to a fresh byte[] before the inbound ring buffer, keeping FixParser pure byte[] with no refcount discipline - MALFORMED (bad/oversized/non-numeric 9=, broken trailer) resyncs to the next 8=; NEED_MORE waits for more bytes - add MAX_FRAME guard and netty-codec dependency (compile scope)
Boundary rule now: FixFrameDecoder may import io.netty; FixParser may not.

test(gateway): cover FixFrameDecoder framing (Step 6)
Drive the Netty-free core on byte[]: frameLength outcomes (complete, NEED_MORE, MALFORMED across bad/empty/oversized 9= and broken trailer) and frameAndEmit over the five build-guide stream cases plus malformed-prefix resync and pure-garbage discard. Two EmbeddedChannel checks confirm the ByteToMessageDecoder wrapper accumulates correctly, including a message split across writes.

Step 6.5: inbound Disruptor wiring (SRS §3.2)
Add the inbound ring buffer so Step 7 has a buffer to produce into.
- pom: add com.lmax:disruptor:4.0.0 (compile scope) - OrderEventFactory: pre-allocates empty OrderEvent slots; isolates the sole com.lmax import in the event package (OrderEvent stays framework-free) - InboundPipeline: single-producer Disruptor<OrderEvent>, one consumer, BlockingWaitStrategy (demo default), 1024-slot ring; exposes the RingBuffer - CapturingOrderHandler (test): reusable snapshot-recording consumer for 6.5 and Step 7; copies fields out to survive slot reuse - InboundPipelineTest: distinct/empty slots, publish round-trip, and slot-reuse (size-1 ring) with no stale-field bleed
